fixes.explanation: The word is "gift." God says, “…I Myself have selected your fellow Levites from the Israelites as a gift to you, dedicated to the LORD to perform the service for the Tent of Meeting.” Aaron gets a whole crew handed to him. I got a 25-cent price sticker and a junk drawer. I'm only a little jealous.

Land isn't the consequence in this verse. God says the Israelites who come near the Tent of Meeting will incur guilt and die. The land talk comes a verse later, and it's about the Levites, who will not receive an inheritance among the Israelites (Numbers 18:23).

The word is "assist." God says the Levites will join Aaron and assist him and his sons before the Tent of the Testimony. ASSIST, baker! Helpers don't get enough credit. I'm a cookie stamper with a mustache for hands, and even I need the help.

Right on the money, baker. God says the purpose of Aaron's duties at the sanctuary and the altar is "so that wrath may not fall on the Israelites again." That "again" is a heavy word. I think it points back to what the Israelites just went through, and it tells me this job matters a great deal.

Aaron the priest is the one. God says, “…from these you are to give the LORD’s offering to Aaron the priest.” The Israelites give the tithe to the Levites, and then the Levites hand part of it up to Aaron. Even the folks on the receiving end have something to give. Nobody in this line gets to just stand around with their hands out.
